Phase 9 exceptions from Gate B (step 2.13, docs/reviews/gate-b-packet.md §8; numbers are median p99 of 3 runs): (1) class-hub rename 16.5 ms vs 16 - cause RTE-002/004 `peers` (routesAffectedBy walks referrers upward, ~10.5 ms); fix: declare peerReads on RTE-002/004 (and audit it); (2) class-hub parent move 46.0 ms (structural: SPC-006 re-runs on 1,400 species + merging ~1,400 findings); (3) review-status change on the like-water hub 21.2 ms per commit (structural: RVW-002 on ~1,000 referrers + finding-store merge); (4) route search dense 17.2 ms this run - untouched code, noise (earlier runs 9.3-12.1 ms), re-check on a quiet machine; (5) validateTouched/validateTouchedByRule without previous state: 38.7-47.1 ms on a 1,000-referrer hub - the compute worker must always pass previous (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Phase 4 note).

Step 2.13: HIER-001, HIER-003, RTE-002 and RTE-004 declare no referencedReads (they walk hierarchies, compositions or routes through derived indexes); REF-006/REF-008, REL-003/005, CUR-004/006, PRS-001/002, HIER-003, RTE-002/004 declare no peerReads. Those rules keep the coarser behaviour.

Step 3.2: snapshot build (0.8 s) and whole restore (3.5 s) run on the main thread at the design tier until Phase 4 hosts them in the compute worker; judged at Gate E. restoreSnapshot does not wait for the restored state to reach IndexedDB (callers flush()).
Phase 5: the app reports a restore or an import as done only after flush() resolves with status saved; until then it shows 'saving'.

Phase 4: replaceState runs validateAll on the main thread (about 2 s of a 3.5 s restore at the design tier; index build about 0.5 s, validateAll about 1.3 s). From Phase 4 the compute worker validates the replica and builds its indexes; replaceState and ADR-033's reload must accept precomputed findings AND prebuilt indexes, so the main thread only swaps state, and boot does not build indexes twice (open() builds them for validateAll and the store builds them again: about 0.45 s at the design tier).
Revision-gap recovery API is built (step 3.3: replaceAll + SaveStatus.failureReason 'revision_gap'); the 'save everything now' button and reading the reason are Phase 5.

Timing decision (step 3.3 review, TEST_STRATEGY §1): tests that assert elapsed milliseconds live in tests/timing and run only through `npm run test:timing` at gates next to bench:baseline; they are not part of `npm run check` or `npm run test:coverage`. Property tests keep their assertions; tests/property/validation-scope.test.ts (P-11) has its per-test timeout raised to 120 s (a resource limit).
Step 3.3: rows that fail L1 are MOVED to quarantine at boot (whole raw value); a Diagnostics repair/restore action for quarantined rows is Phase 9.

Phase 5 wiring for multi-tab (step 3.4, no UI yet): store with readOnly: follower.isReadOnly + follower.attach; attachWriteQueue after a writer boot and after the promoted event; read-only and single-tab banners; handle loaded, promotion_failed, reload_failed, row_rejected. The Playwright halves of ADV-039 are Gate E.

A tab whose promotion was refused (newer schema, failed migration, damaged meta) does not ask for the lock again, so it is not promoted when the next writer closes. Decide in Phase 5 (retry, or reload to retry).

Step 3.4 constants for reviewer confirmation: 2,000 changed IDs per change message, 512 characters per ID, follower backlog 100, 20 reported rejected rows per reload. The hub-edit applyRemote costs about 400 ms on the main thread (about the writer's own commit of it); the follower's reload is a full L1 + index build + validateAll (about 2 s at the design tier): Phase 4 moves both to the compute worker.
